expectations.text: Describes checking the document's imports field to see if the library is already imported before attempting to add it
expectations.evidence: Step 1: 'The current imports object — specifically, whether ./design/system.lib.pen is already present'. Step 4: 'If get_editor_state showed the library is not yet in the document's imports, I add it now' and 'If the library was already imported, I skip this step entirely.'

expectations.text: Instantiates Button and Input via ref nodes — does NOT describe building them from primitives (frame + text, etc.)
expectations.evidence: Step 9 shows explicit type: 'ref' ops for emailField, passwordField, and submitButton. Commentary states: 'Components are instantiated as ref nodes, not rebuilt from primitives. The Button and Input components from your library update automatically when the library changes; hand-built lookalikes don't.'

expectations.text: Describes using snapshot_layout or batch_get to verify structure and bindings BEFORE reaching for get_screenshot
expectations.evidence: Step 10 defines a 4-rung ladder: Rung 2 is snapshot_layout, Rung 3 is batch_get on instances, Rung 4 is get_screenshot. Tool table confirms steps 9 and 10 are snapshot_layout and batch_get, step 11 is get_screenshot — explicit ordering enforced.

expectations.text: Uses at most one get_screenshot call as final sign-off, scoped to the form or card subtree (NOT the page frame or document root)
expectations.evidence: Step 10 Rung 4: 'get_screenshot(nodeId: "<form-id>")' scoped to the form node. Closing statement: 'Total screenshots: 1, scoped to the smallest meaningful subtree. No mid-flight screenshots, no full-canvas screenshots.'

claims.claim: The response describes reading library component IDs via batch_get before referencing them in ref ops
claims.evidence: Step 3 explicitly calls batch_get on the library file and states: 'I never guess at component names — ButtonPrimary vs Button vs btn-primary is a real distinction and the server rejects a mismatched ref.'

claims.claim: The response states that descendant override keys are sourced from the real library tree, not guessed
claims.evidence: Step 9 commentary: 'descendants overrides target child IDs from the library component's actual tree (learned in step 3). I don't guess these names.'

claims.claim: Colors use $variable references rather than raw hex values
claims.evidence: Step 9 ops use $surface, $colorPrimary, $textXl, $textPrimary, $textSm. Commentary: 'Colors reference $variable names, not raw hex. This preserves light/dark theme behavior.'

claims.claim: The response handles the 'transport not connected' error case explicitly
claims.evidence: Step 1: 'If it errors with transport not connected to app: desktop, I stop immediately and tell you to open the Pencil desktop app or IDE extension — I don't silently fall back to anything else.'

claims.claim: The import is added via batch_design U op that merges with existing imports rather than overwriting them
claims.evidence: Step 4: 'I merge with any existing imports (read the current imports object from get_editor_state and combine, never clobber).'

suggestions.reason: All four assertions are satisfied by a well-structured plan document, but none verify that the batch_get call on the library (Step 3) precedes the batch_design import op (Step 4). An agent could pass all assertions by describing ref instantiation without ever reading real component IDs from the library first — which is the core failure mode (guessing ref names). Consider adding: 'Describes reading component IDs from the library via batch_get BEFORE constructing ref ops, rather than hard-coding assumed names.'

suggestions.assertion: Instantiates Button and Input via ref nodes — does NOT describe building them from primitives (frame + text, etc.)
suggestions.reason: This assertion would also pass if the response mentioned ref nodes but only used them for one component and built the other from scratch. Tightening to 'ALL interactive components (Button AND Input) are instantiated as ref nodes' would make it more discriminating.

No assertion covers the import merge behavior — a common failure mode is clobbering existing imports when adding a new one. The transcript correctly describes merging (Step 4), but no eval checks for it.

eval_feedback.overall: Strong evals that target the key behaviors. The main gap is that passing all four assertions does not guarantee the agent read actual component IDs from the library before using them in refs — that intermediate step is the most important guard against silent failures in production.
